text:
maria: Heads-up — Sunridge (acct SNR-501) hit our collections today. Invoice INV-2026-114 (due 2026-02-10) still unpaid, $48,720. Customer says their card was declined and disputes a portion ($12,500) as ‘unauthorized vendor charges’. We need to decide: immediate suspension, short payment plan, or escalate to legal. Any objections to offering a 60-day installment plan with first payment today?
clare: Thanks Maria. Sales flagged this one as strategic — they want to avoid churn if dispute is small. Do we have past-chargebacks for them?
raj: CX notes show Sunridge opened a support ticket about unexpected line-item on 2026-02-08. They didn’t authorize a pilot add-on. We asked for evidence but haven’t received it.
billing-bot: Payment attempt on 2026-02-11 failed: CC decline. Last successful payment: 2025-12-30. Past due balance: $48,720. Reattempt schedule: 2026-02-18.
maria: No previous chargebacks. This is first disputed amount. Sales (clare) recommends split: let them keep base service, suspend add-on features until resolved. That would reduce churn risk. Thoughts on putting a hold on new API keys until partial payment received?
clare: Agree on hold for add-on only. Sales can accept a 3-installment plan (20% now, 40% in 30d, 40% in 60d) if legal OK. They want a credit note for the disputed $12.5k if investigation finds it was erroneously billed.
tyler: From legal POV: we can accept a conditional installment plan — include clause that payments do not waive our right to collect disputed portion after investigation. Also require written confirmation from customer accepting the plan and agreeing to arbitration timeline.
maria: Drafting an email + payment schedule. Proposed message to customer: short plan summary + link to self-serve ACH or card update + 5 business-day window to accept before we escalate. Ok to proceed?
raj: Suggest adding a soft reminder escalation: automated reminders on day 3 and day 7. CX available to jump in if they respond.
clare: Sales will offer to waive late fees for good-faith first instalment today. That helps optics.
tyler: Fine on waiving late fees for now. Keep audit trail. If they don’t respond by EOD +5 business, we escalate to collections/legal.
maria: OK I’ll send draft and paste here for sign-off. Draft: "Hi Sunridge — we received your dispute. To avoid service disruption while we investigate, we’re offering a conditional 3-part payment plan: 20% due now ($9,744), 40% in 30 days, 40% in 60 days. Please confirm acceptance within 5 business days and update payment method via this secure link: https://pay.redwood.example/snr-501. Note: payments do not forfeit our right to collect any disputed amounts pending investigation. If we don’t hear back, we’ll proceed with temporary add-on suspension and collections escalation." Approve to send?
clare: Approve from Sales.
tyler: Approve from Legal (suggest minor tweak: change "do not forfeit" to "do not constitute a waiver of our rights").
raj: CX approve — can monitor thread and jump in if they reply.
maria: Thanks all. I’ll apply the 3-installment invoice adjustment, set up automated reminders, flag account for add-on suspension on 2026-02-20 if no response, and send the message. Will paste copy of sent email here.
clare: Thanks — ping me if they ask for extended terms beyond 60 days.
maria: Pasted sent email below: "Sent to billing@sunridge.ai on 2026-02-12 16:12 UTC — Subject: Important: Invoice INV-2026-114 — proposed payment plan". Reopening reattempt schedule and monitoring.
raj: Noted. I’ll slot CX follow-up in case they accept.
clare: Good work team :thumbsup:
